title: Rushing to inhabit the next chapter

captions.energy: Hurrying the end of old routines

meaning: Creating a new routine can bring shared enthusiasm, but support needs time to grow after you leave familiar arrangements behind.
text: Making changes at home can bring a sense of moving forward together: useful comforts appear, and life takes a new shape. The Empress in the physical position of Muladhara describes this creative work. Death in energy tests your footing through a demand to finish decisively with the previous routine, leaving no time to settle into change. The Chariot in emotions enjoys progress: it feels good to know a step has been taken. Yet when success is sought only further ahead, domestic stability cannot grow where you have already arrived together.

For example, you clear old supplies from the kitchen and reorganise familiar storage. There is more room, but your hand still reaches towards the old cup shelf, while you already want another alteration. **Change becomes support when you have time to live within it.** A few quiet evenings show what actually works for two. They allow the shared result to enter ordinary life and become more than another stage successfully completed.

The difficulty is taking that familiar movement of the hand as evidence that the past still holds too tightly. You may remove more things, hurry the transition and insist more strongly on the new order. Home keeps changing, but simple tasks become harder to do without strain. Support grows firmer when ending the old allows gradual familiarity with the new, without turning ordinary adjustment into an obstacle to your shared progress.
